Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and I attached our privacy questionnaire for detail.

1) Roles: MedSync will be Controller for patient clinical records, and we expect Redwood to be a Processor for the inference/transcription pipeline. We will still want explicit controller/processor language in the DPA.

2) PII/PHI scope: primary items = patient name, MRN (medical record number), DOB, provider IDs, device serial IDs, audio recordings/transcripts (which contain clinical notes). We may also surface limited insurance identifiers in some workflows. 

3) Retention: regulatory retention applies to clinical records (7 years for adults per state law); raw audio can be short-lived. Preferred default: keep transcripts + structured extraction for 7 years, raw audio 90 days unless flagged. If Redwood cannot separate tiers, that’s important for the contract.

4) Logging: we require per-request audit logs with user/service identity, timestamp, requester IP, and whether PII was redacted. Exportable CSV and 1-year retention is our minimum; 7-year retention for admin-level logs only if the logs are tied to clinical record changes.

5) Subprocessors & certs: please provide current subprocessor list (SOC2 + HIPAA controls where applicable). We will need proof of SOC2 Type II. We’ll also need to understand how Redwood notifies customers of subprocessor changes.

6) Breach notice: our SLT prefers 48 hours for initial notice; 72 hours is acceptable only with strong interim alerting (e.g., acknowledgement within 24 hours that an investigation has started).

Attached: medsync-privacy-q1.xlsx with field-level mapping. Happy to chat if anything needs more context.

—Sarah
Sarah Patel
Director, Privacy & Compliance, MedSync Health

Thanks for the context, Jordan — good notes. High-level legal guidance and next steps below.

Summary guidance
- Roles: Redwood will be treated as a Processor for the described inference/transcription services — standard DPA language applies. We will formalize that in the DPA and include data processing instructions.
- BAA: If MedSync will process or direct processing of PHI (protected health information), a BAA is required under HIPAA. We can attach our BAA as an addendum to the DPA; I’ll prepare a draft tailored to the stated scope.
- Breach notice: Redwood’s standard commercial DPA currently specifies an initial notification window of 72 hours for confirmed breaches. We can agree to a 48-hour initial notification in enterprise negotiations provided we include a contractual carve for preliminary investigatory alerts (e.g., acknowledgement/initial findings within 24 hours).
- Retention: supporting tiered retention (transcripts + structured records 7 years; raw audio 90 days) is feasible but may require configuration flags / per-customer retention policies. Engineering will need to confirm whether that’s supported on Hosted vs Dedicated/Private. If not, Dedicated or Private deployment may be recommended for strict separation.
- Logging: we can provide per-request audit logs with requester identity, timestamp, and request metadata. Default retention on Hosted is 1 year for request logs; export capability available via Console/API. For 7-year admin-level retention we typically recommend Dedicated retention policies or log export/archival to customer-managed storage.
- Subprocessors: I attached current subprocessor CSV and a link to our published list. We notify customers of material changes via email + Console notification; we can offer 30 days’ notice for contractual commitments. SOC2 Type II report is available under NDA — we can trigger the SOC2 share after an NDA is in place.

Action items
- Jordan/Marissa: confirm whether we should propose a 48-hour initial-notify clause with the investigatory carve (I recommend yes for momentum but flag it as negotiable).
- Ops/Eng: please confirm feasibility for per-data-class retention on Hosted by EOD Thu. If not possible, specify the minimum required deployment (Dedicated/Private) and approximate timeline/est effort.
- Legal: I’ll circulate a BAA + DPA addendum draft by Fri with optional 48h clause and the subprocessor notification language. Once we have MedSync’s field mapping (their questionnaire), I’ll annotate which fields are likely PHI and where the BAA scope applies.
